title: NAILS status --json
description: Machine-readable status envelope (contract version 2): one document with schema_version, command, ok, and data (a report), or error together with data when reading the record was refused, so no report could be built. `place` is where the machine is, `unknown` in that second case; `attention` names the one thing, if any, that needs the operator. `ok` is true only when the exit code is 0 or 9. A Ctrl+C or SIGTERM before the result is the shared cancel shape: the error `cancelled`, no data, exit 130. An internal error is the error `internal_error`, exit 1.

place.description: Where the machine is: the plain decoy, the hidden session, or an activation in flight. `unknown` only with an error: reading the record was refused, so nothing was established.

attention.description: The one thing that needs the operator, or null when nothing does. A hidden root without a way back (`no_way_back`) and an interrupted activation (`interrupted`) come first, each with its own remediation; then `record_unreadable` (the state file could not be read or trusted), in every place, ahead of the rest.

reason.description: Why the place needs attention, when a reason is known. With the switch_refused attention, the reason the switch gave.

accepted_decoy_storage.description: Why the hidden root is not a volume of its own, when the session's activation accepted that with --allow-decoy-storage.

hidden_root_covered_by.description: The source of a filesystem mounted over the hidden volume, which now receives every file saved under the hidden root.

policy_mounts.description: The decoy filesystems the fstab policy placed in the hidden root.

masked_units.description: The decoy units masked in the hidden root: the swap and the decoy filesystems it keeps off where no boot target requires them, or where it cannot skip them (those are in required_units too, with why), and the units that fail or do nothing there (the boot-loader units, systemd-remount-fs.service, systemd-growfs-root.service). A unit a boot target requires that is skipped is not masked and is listed in required_units alone. The generator masks are not listed.

required_units.description: The units a boot target (local-fs.target, remote-fs.target, swap.target) requires that the session keeps from starting, each with how and why. `skipped`: the unit gets a runtime drop-in whose start condition never holds, so the target is still reached (`required_at_boot`). `masked`: the unit never loads, and a target that still requires it is not reached; its device was not there at the entry or at the switch (`device_absent`, with `device`), NAILS could not tell what the unit is or what it pulls in (`undetermined`), the fstab lines or unit files the hidden systemd may read for it disagree (`conflicting_lines`), or a drop-in of the decoy's would undo its skip, one named like the skip's drop-in that systemd reads in its place or one that sorts after it and resets the start conditions (`skip_undone`), or its skip would pull in a mount, swap or automount the session neither keeps off nor puts in place, such as the mount of a parent directory or one its Requires= or RequiresMountsFor= names, which the hidden systemd would mount from the decoy's disk (`pulls_in_mount`). Read from the session plan in /run; empty when there is none.

decoy_persistent.description: Whether the decoy keeps a persistent log/audit store (a persistent journald journal, or active rsyslog/syslog-ng/auditd).

decoy_kdump_armed.description: Whether kdump is armed on the decoy (a loaded crash kernel, or an enabled or active kdump-tools.service or kdump.service), or /sys/kernel/kexec_crash_loaded cannot be read or holds neither 0 nor 1. Activation refuses it without --allow-persistent-decoy. False in a hidden session.

switch_refusal.description: Why and when the last session switch was refused: the soft-reboot stayed on the root it was on. Kept on the hidden volume (a refused entry, shown once the volume is open again) or in /run (a refused way back, shown in the hidden session) until the next activate or deactivate arms its own switch.
